answer: To stop sybil farms, each agent must forge a unique hollow proof by sequentially processing the shared wharf log. The k-th identity waits on the single wharf queue and re-forges a hollow hash over the cumulative prior proofs (chain length proportional to k). Clones cannot parallelize because only one forge runs on the shared wharf clock at a time; attacker cost therefore scales as O(k^2) sequential forge operations that grow with every additional fake.
